items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Bernie and I played muted except for those two occasions.

ctx.x: We had to do a musical show at a certain time every night and the number Teddy had chosen for me to feature was Gershwin's "I've Got Plenty of Nothing". We did our feature numbers on the dance floor in front of the band. The bandstand was very nice and Teddy's piano was on the floor with the band behind him.

There was also three nights a week when we had to broadcast. We could not blow very loud except during our show and for the radio, so Bernie and I played muted except for those two occasions. And I used to turn my back at times when I had a solo on an up tempo number, and blow at J.C. who sat in back of me. It may not have looked very nice but there is a certain amount of push in fast numbers that made it almost impossible for me to play if I had to hold back and use a mute at the same time.

One night we were playing "Sweet Georgia Brown" and on the last chorus, J.C. was really pushing and the number was swinging more that night than ever before. I had a feeling that I could never have had if Yank Porter had been on drums. So I turned towards J.C. and blowed the way I felt and ended on a high F.
